Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Posen is mostly pre-1978 stock, and that changes the setup

Of the 1,721 housing units counted in Posen, 71.8 percent went up before 1980. There is no pre-1978 bucket, so 1980 is the nearest line the Census draws for Posen. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Posen at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 6-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Posen.

The useful question is not whether the rule applies to your Posen house. At 65.9 percent pre-1970 it very likely does. The useful question is what the containment and the cleanup are actually going to look like in your rooms, and it is a fair one to ask anybody.

No lead-safe certification is claimed anywhere on this site, because no number has been provided to put here. The panel below leaves the slot open on purpose, in Posen and everywhere else. Ask any contractor for theirs.

Why the town line matters here

The nearest place on this site to Posen is Dixmoor, 1.0 miles away. Same drive, different job. The figures that separate them are median home value ($172,800 against $75,500); share of units in buildings of two or more (12.3 percent against 5.8 percent); owner households (1,172 against 587).

Why two houses in Posen do not price the same

Aluminum and steel are the surprise on 1960-era houses: soffit, fascia wrap, gutters and often the garage door. They take paint perfectly well and they take it badly if nobody cleans the chalk off first. On the 87.7 percent of Posen that is detached houses, that one step is the difference between an exterior that lasts and one that comes off in sheets. With 1,172 owner households and 464 renting, this is two markets in one place: owners doing a room or an elevation at a time, and small landlords wanting a unit turned around cleanly between tenants. They are not the same quote.

What should be on a written quote in Posen

  • Whole elevations. 87.7 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Distance, stated. Posen is 9.9 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Posen is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 71.8 percent of housing in Posen was built before 1980, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is ranch, raised ranch and split-level, usually masonry to the sill line with frame gables above. Almost all the exterior paint in Posen sits above head height, which is why the work takes longer than the surface area suggests.

That reading comes from two numbers on this page and nothing else: a median build year of 1960 and a structure split of 87.7 percent detached, 0 percent attached and 12.3 percent in buildings of two or more.

That is inference and it is labeled as one. Wall material in Posen is not collected by any source behind this page, so there is no honest figure to put on it. Look at your own house and you will know more than this paragraph does.

Questions

Asked about Posen

Who actually shows up in Posen?

Mike Walsh owns the company, walks the job and stays on it while our crew works. Call 708-935-4289. It is worth saying because on a job this size the gap between whoever measured it and whoever turns up is where most of the disappointment comes from.

Can it be done a room at a time?

It can. Splitting a 6-room house into phases is normal and it is priced as phases rather than as a discount on the whole. The trade-off is setup time, because masking and protecting a room costs the same whether it is one room or the fourth.

What changes the price most on a house here?

Prep. Housing here runs to a 1960 median, which means several coats are already on the woodwork and some of them were put on badly. Undoing that is the expensive part, and it is the part that a fast number leaves out and a slow one explains.

Does the lead-safe rule apply to my house in Posen?

Probably, and the honest answer is that your build year decides it rather than the town. 71.8 percent of housing units in Posen went up before 1980, so most addresses here land on the pre-1978 side of the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. It applies to work that disturbs paint, at roughly six square feet per room inside or twenty square feet outside, and to any window replacement. Check the year on your own address and ask whoever quotes you how they handle it.
